ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which pair differs in the sounds /s/ and /ʃ/? (1 mark)
   A. sea and she
   B. sit and seat
   C. live and leave
   D. go and no

2. Why do flies spread germs? (1 mark)
   A. They sleep on beds
   B. They land on waste and then on food
   C. They drink clean water
   D. They eat all the soap

3. Which of these is a coordinating conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. but
   C. tidy
   D. broom

4. What is a descriptive composition? (1 mark)
   A. A list of numbers
   B. A story with a problem to solve
   C. A letter to a friend
   D. Writing that paints a picture of a person, place, object or activity

5. Which is the best question for the answer 'In the school hall'? (1 mark)
   A. Whose hall is it?
   B. Where did they practise?
   C. When did they practise?
   D. Who practised?

6. Which question has the correct word order after 'where'? (1 mark)
   A. Where you keep the ball?
   B. Where do you keeps the ball?
   C. Where you do keep the ball?
   D. Where do you keep the ball?

7. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'very pretty'? (1 mark)
   A. beatiful
   B. beautiful
   C. beutiful
   D. butiful

8. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'apart, not together'? (1 mark)
   A. separete
   B. separate
   C. seprate
   D. seperate

9. Which word begins with the cluster 'br'? (1 mark)
   A. sweep
   B. broom
   C. clap
   D. grass

10. How should you read a poem with rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. Tap the beat and stress the strong syllables
   B. Whisper every line
   C. Read as fast as you can
   D. Skip the rhymes

11. Which is the negative of 'I have eaten'? (1 mark)
   A. I not have eaten.
   B. I has not eaten.
   C. I have not eaten.
   D. I do not have eaten.

12. What is a diary? (1 mark)
   A. A personal record of what happens to you each day
   B. A letter to a friend
   C. A dictionary
   D. A newspaper

13. Which tense do we usually use for earlier events in a diary? (1 mark)
   A. Future tense
   B. Question form
   C. Command
   D. Past tense

14. Which word ends with the sound /ŋ/? (1 mark)
   A. sin
   B. sum
   C. sing
   D. sun

15. What sounds does the letter x usually make in 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. /z/
   B. /gz/
   C. /f/
   D. /ks/

16. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. An advert
   B. The writer's name
   C. A photograph
   D. A short bold title that tells what a news story is about

17. Which sentence uses the correct preposition for a public vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. He is by the bus in.
   B. He is on the bus.
   C. He is in the bus.
   D. He is at the bus inside.

18. Which preposition means 'facing'? (1 mark)
   A. behind
   B. opposite
   C. among
   D. between

19. Which is the correct spelling of the word for a person who keeps money records? (1 mark)
   A. accountent
   B. acounttant
   C. acountant
   D. accountant

20. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'glad'? (1 mark)
   A. happpy
   B. hapy
   C. happy
   D. hapie

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write four sentences about cleaning your classroom that use and, but, so and or. (4 marks)

22. Explain the difference between 'who' and 'whose'. Give one question for each. (3 marks)

23. Explain the difference between 'I have eaten' and 'I had eaten when he came.' (3 marks)

24. Write four sentences to advise classmates on keeping the school toilets clean. (4 marks)

25. Write a short speech of four sentences about protecting a river. (4 marks)

26. Write three sentences using three of these words: because, different, address, favourite, tomorrow. (3 marks)

27. Write a question for each answer: (a) 'It is at the stadium.' (b) 'The coach.' (2 marks)

28. Join with a suitable conjunction: 'I was tired. I finished sweeping.' (2 marks)

29. Give two safety rules for using the internet. (2 marks)

30. Replace each plain word with a better describing word: nice room, dirty clothes, good smell. Write the new phrases. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — sea and she
   'Sea' has /s/ and 'she' has /ʃ/.

2. B — They land on waste and then on food
   Flies carry germs from waste to food.

3. B — but
   'But' joins words or sentences.

4. D — Writing that paints a picture of a person, place, object or activity
   It describes so that the reader can imagine.

5. B — Where did they practise?
   The answer names a place.

6. D — Where do you keep the ball?
   The helping verb 'do' comes before the subject.

7. B — beautiful
   Beautiful is spelt b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u-l.

8. B — separate
   Remember 'a rat' in separate.

9. B — broom
   'Broom' begins with b and r.

10. A — Tap the beat and stress the strong syllables
   Follow the beat with your voice.

11. C — I have not eaten.
   Add not after have.

12. A — A personal record of what happens to you each day
   A diary records events and feelings.

13. D — Past tense
   Events that already happened use the past tense.

14. C — sing
   'Sing' ends with /ŋ/.

15. D — /ks/
   In 'box', x says k and s together.

16. D — A short bold title that tells what a news story is about
   The headline gives the subject of a story.

17. B — He is on the bus.
   We say 'on the bus'.

18. B — opposite
   'The post office is opposite the bank.'

19. D — accountant
   Accountant has a double c.

20. C — happy
   Happy has a double p.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences, each with the named conjunction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Who' asks about a person: Who is the coach? 'Whose' asks about the owner: Whose ball is this?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'I have eaten' says the eating is finished and it matters now. 'I had eaten when he came' says I finished eating before he came, in the past.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for the time link.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap after using the toilet. Do not throw rubbish in the latrine. Keep the door closed. Tell the teacher about any damage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two points such as not throwing rubbish in the river and planting trees on its bank, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each element.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences using the words with correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) Where is it? (b) Who is the man with the whistle?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable conjunction (but or yet) and 1 for the comma.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not share personal details; tell an adult if something worries you; use approved sites.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: bright, tidy room; muddy, crumpled clothes; fresh smell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
